recipes.name: Double Layer Pumpkin Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can solid pack pumpkin puree
2 (3.5 ounce) packages instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Pour milk for pumpkin layer into large bowl. Add pumpkin puree, pudding mix, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves and whisk until thoroughly mixed. Let sit until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, beat cream cheese, milk, and sugar for cheesecake layer in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Gently stir in whipped topping.
Spoon into graham cracker crust and spread into an even layer.
Spread thickened pumpkin mixture over top. Cover and refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Double Layer Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: This double layer pumpkin pie takes two dessert faves and layers them into one. Rich, creamy cheesecake or spiced pumpkin pie? You don't have to choose!

review.reviewBody: CHILL THE CRUST BEFORE ADDING THE FIRST LAYER.AFTER YOU HAVE ADDED THE FIRST LAYER, CHILL AGAIN BEFORE ADDING THE SECOND. THIS HELPS THE PIE TO SET AND WILL HELP AVOID MIXING OF THE LAYERS AS MENTIONED IN OTHER REVIEWS.

Ok LOVE this pie. The modifications are 8oz of cream cheese and 2 Tb sugar with no milk (along w the whipped topping). Freeze it after first layer for about 10 min. Put 3/4 cup cold evaporated milk. and 1 and 2/3 packages of vanilla pudding mix. Then mix it together until smooth. Then put 3/4 of the 15 oz can of pumpkin in it(not cup the can). Put 1/4-1/2 t pumpkin pie spice. and 1/4-1/2 t cinnamon. Do this and your pie will be perfect. Not runny or too sweet, not too much filling and will taste pretty much like pumpkin pie. For the rest of the pudding mix and canned pumpkin you probably could make a mouse out of it but haven't tried it. Just saying.

Out of all the double layer pumpkin pie recipes this one is the best. It does not use pumpkin pie spice. This recipe uses spices that you can custom to your family's taste. I did make a change in the order I put it together. I first make the cream cheese layer and put it in the extra 2 pieces ready made crust from the elf. I cover it with the plastic lid turned over that comes on the crust and put in fridge. I then can make the pumpkin layer with the same mixing bowl and beaters. No cleaning necessary. I think I used the whole 8 oz of cream cheese by accident and it was still good. I also used half the small tub of Cool Whip. Then I use the rest of the Cool Whip on the top to decorate. I can still use the plastic lid to cover the pie for any left overs( haha) you might have. I don't put nuts because the pie is to melt in your mouth if you wait. The longer you wait the moistier the crust gets. I have been known to make the cream cheese layer and make the pumpkin layer the next day. You should wash the bowl if you do.

Update 11/19/11: Added 1/4 cup finely chopped pecans to my home made graham cracker crust..The crust was almost as good as the pie! Remember to only use 3/4 cup of milk (I use half and half or cream) or it will be too soupy. 
Update: 11/11/10 Made a sugar-free version. Used sf vanilla pudding, sf cool whip, and splenda for sugar. Added a couple of extra splenda packets to pumpkin mix. Got rave reviews! Tried again and this time only used 3/4 cup of half and half. Excellent results-not runny at all! Made my own pie crust though-used the recipe on the back of the Honey Maid Graham cracker crumbs box and used a smaller pie pan like an old Bakers Square tin. If you have left over pumpking filling, it can be served and eaten as a "pumpkin mousse". Five people asked me for the recipe and one said it was the best pumpkin pie she ever had!

Great pumpkin pie recipe. I used one package or vanilla pudding and one package of pumpkin pudding thats always in the stores this time of year. I think I will try reducing the milk to 3/4 cup so it sets firmer. I also took the 4 oz of cream cheese and beat it together with 1/2 C confect sugar then in another bowl I beat 1/2 cup heavy cream to a whipped cream consistency. Then folded that into the cream cheese mixture . spread it into the pie shell and chilled it first before adding the pumpkin filling mixture.

Have been using this recipe for many, many years! Agree that once the cream cheese and whipping cream base is mixed that you refrigerate it for at least an hour prior to adding the pumpkin layer. Also will add -- 3.25% homogenized milk and 1 3/4 cups of pumpkin filling works well in this recipe which will give you more than enough if using a pre-made 9" graham cracker pie shell. As you will have excess filling left over use it to make at least ten to twelve small pastry tarts. 
Tarts: Bake first and let cool. As you will need extra cream cheese filling; cut ingredients in half and prepare the same way as you did for the pie. Line baked tarts with the mixture and refrigerate. Add excess pumpkin layer on top. Refrigerate as well until use.

I have no idea how all this is supposed to fit in a 9 inch pie crust. The first time I made it, I followed the instructions and ended up with a bunch of leftover filling. This time I did not add 1 1/2 cups of whipped topping to the cream cheese mixture. Instead I only mixed the cream cheese, sugar, and milk together, placed it in the crust, and spread a thin layer of whipped topping over that. I put that in the freezer for a few hours, then mixed the pumpkin with the remaining ingredients and spread it over all. I refrigerated that until time to eat, and then added the whipped topping on the individual slices. It worked much better this way.

I was looking for something more exciting than plain old heavy, dense pumpkin pie. This was perfect, and so easy! I sprinkled some chopped pecans with cinnamon & sugar and toasted them in the oven for 15 min at 325, then sprinkled some on top of crust before adding cream cheese layer. Then I chilled that for 30 min before adding pumpkin layer, and sprinkled more pecans on top. Refrigerated overnight and it was totally awesome!!

I tweaked this recipe quite a bit based on other reviewers comments. I used 8 oz cream cheese,2 tbsp sugar, the topping as listed, and no milk. Chilled the store bought crust, then put the first layer in then put the pie in the freezer while fixing the second layer. The second layer I started with half of the pumpkin and half and half - not milk, then played to get a good texture.... ended up with 3/4 can pumpkin, the 2 packages of vanilla pudding, 1 tsp vanilla, a 1/2 to 2/3 cup of half and half, 2 tsp cinnamon, and 1/2-3/4 tsp nutmeg, plus a couple of globs of whipped cream topping. This made a nice spreadable but thick layer with a spicy pumpkin taste. Brought it to the office, told folks it was in the fridge, and I have been stopped repeatedly with compliments. I have been told I have to make it again for Christmas... :) Not really cheesecake, not pudding, I called it pumpkin cream pie.

Absolutely Brilliant. I made this for thanksgiving dinner, and it was AMAZING. Everyone loved it. Although, make sure to chill the crust before adding the first layer, and then chill it after adding the first layer to help prevent the layers from mixing. This recipe is insanely easy to make, and I would definitely recommend this to anyone.

Loved this pie! There are a couple changes that I would make. First You need to specify that the 1tbsp is for the cream cheese mixture. Its obvious to some but after reading other reviews maybe not. Also I believe the amount is off on the cream cheese. 8oz worked much better mixed with 2tbsp sugar and 2tbsp milk. Also Mix in about 1/2 of the pumpkin mixture into the cream cheese to give it a pumpkin flavor instead of just a sweetend cream cheese flavor. Tasted much better this way.

I followed the suggestions of other reviewers and froze my crust. Once frozen I then added the cream cheese layer. I froze it again for two more hours. Then I added the pumpkin layer. I froze it again, but it never did quite set up. The cheesecake layer tasted just like whipped cream, no tang at all from the cream cheese. I liked it, but not enough to make it again.

This is a great and was a hit with the whole family. I make my own vanilla pudding mix (Homemade Vanilla Pudding from this site) instead of the packaged stuff, and I sub real whipped cream for the "frozen whipped topping" to avoid all the additives that I can't pronounce. Thanks for a great recipe!
Excellent recipe. The family loves it.
My copy from mom's was confusing it had 1 cup plus 1 tsp of milk...It didn't say to spilt them Thanks.
Best pumpkin pie ever. I used the suggestions in reviews. Definitely freeze the bottom layer before adding the pumpkin layer.

I haven't cut into it to taste it yet, but it turned out just fine. I didn't read all the comments before making about the layers not setting right and it being soupy. I didn't encounter that at all. I did notice the cream cheese layer is super thin. So, if I make this again I would either double the cream cheese layer or just use 8oz of cream cheese instead of 4oz. I did taste the pumpkin layer from my scrapper and it was nice and spicy! I can't wait to try it out at Thanksgiving tomorrow.

I make this every year, as my husband loves it! but this time I changed it up a bit, only because in error I used the whole tub of cool whip instead of just 1-1/2 cups. That made it a less thick consistency. Rather that put it on the bottom, I used it for the top layer instead! When I make it the way the recipe directs. I used to put the remaining cool whip on the top…but this way it just made a thicker layer of the cream cheese mixture and tasted just as good!!! 👍

First off I use 1/2 and 1/2 instead of milk it will hold up better. I have been making this for years as a child I didn't like pumpkin pie so I make this and I call it child friendly ( who doesn't like pudding )cause my 4 kids love it as do I. I only use 4oz cream cheese and folding is the key. If you mix instead of fold that's where people go wrong. Take the time to gently fold it will make it better
